scenario: Alterion 系统设计面，问你怎么给这个 API 限流。你想说用 token bucket、允许短突发到桶容量，但上次卡在 "we we limit the rate somehow"。
scenario_en: In an Alterion system-design round you're asked how you'd rate-limit the API. You want to say a token bucket allows short bursts up to the bucket size, but last time you stalled on "we we limit the rate somehow."
q: 想说「用 token bucket，按固定速率补令牌、允许突发到桶容量」，该怎么说出口？
q_en: How do you say "a token bucket refills at a fixed rate but allows a burst up to the bucket size" out loud?
options: We use a token bucket — it refills at a steady rate but allows a burst up to the bucket size.
We add a rate-limit machine, a token barrel, it drop the token when too many request come in.
So so we kind of limit the rate, we we count the requests, and if it's too many we we block some, some of them...
The system shall admit requests only when a token is available, with tokens replenished at a fixed constant rate.
tradeoff: 允许突发 vs 绝对匀速：token bucket 放行桶容量内的突发，leaky bucket 把输出削成固定速率。
why: 地道说法是 token bucket：按固定速率补令牌、允许突发到桶容量；leaky bucket 则匀速漏出、削平所有突发。
why_en: It's a token bucket — refills at a fixed rate but allows a burst up to the bucket size, whereas a leaky bucket drains at a constant rate.
whenOtherWins: 如果你要的是绝对平滑、不允许任何突发，就该说 leaky bucket 匀速漏出，而不是 token bucket。
options_en: We use a token bucket — it refills at a steady rate but allows a burst up to the bucket size.
We add a rate-limit machine, a token barrel, it drop the token when too many request come in.
So so we kind of limit the rate, we we count the requests, and if it's too many we we block some, some of them...
The system shall admit requests only when a token is available, with tokens replenished at a fixed constant rate.

token barrel 生造词，搭配全错。
so so / block some 打转，没术语。
shall admit ... replenished 书面腔。
optionMeanings_en: Names token bucket, refill plus burst cap.
"Token barrel" is invented; collocation off.
Loops on "so so / block some," no term.
"Shall admit… replenished" reads like a spec.
optionScenarioImpacts: 对方听出你懂突发与匀速的区别。
术语走形，像没真配过限流。
对方还在等你说出机制。
太正式，像念算法定义。

Mangled term; sounds unpracticed.
They're still waiting for the mechanism.
Too formal — reciting an algorithm definition.
optionDirectness: 抓住 token bucket 加突发上限。
错在生造词，搭配不地道。
错在打转，零信息。
错在语域，书面体僵硬。
optionDirectness_en: Nails token bucket plus the burst cap.
Wrong: invented term, unnatural collocation.
Wrong: pure loop, says nothing.
Wrong register — written style feels stiff.

termDefinitions.meaning: 令牌桶：按固定速率往桶里放令牌，每个请求消耗一个令牌，桶里攒的令牌允许短时突发，直到桶被掏空。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A token bucket refills tokens at a fixed rate; each request spends one, so saved-up tokens allow short bursts up to the bucket size.

termDefinitions.meaning: 漏桶：请求排进桶里、以固定速率匀速漏出，把输出削成恒定速率，不放任何突发过去。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A leaky bucket queues requests and drains them at a constant rate, smoothing output and allowing no bursts.

termDefinitions.meaning: 限流器：控制单位时间内允许多少请求通过，超出就拒绝或排队，保护下游不被打垮。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A rate limiter caps how many requests are allowed per unit time, rejecting or queuing the rest to protect downstream.

scenario: Gamma 后端面，问你怎么把请求按 URL 路径分到不同服务。你想说需要 L7 负载均衡、能读 HTTP，但上次把 L4 L7 说反了。
scenario_en: In a Gamma backend round you're asked how to route requests to different services by URL path. You want to say you need an L7 load balancer that reads HTTP, but last time you mixed up L4 and L7.
q: 想说「需要 L7 负载均衡，它读 HTTP 请求、能按路径或 host 路由」，该怎么说？
q_en: How do you say "we need an L7 load balancer — it reads the HTTP request so it can route by path or host"?
options: We use the layer-four balancer to read the URL and send it to the right service by the path.
So so it depends, we we route the traffic, based on the, based on the path I think, so the higher one, the higher one...
We need an L7 load balancer — it reads the HTTP request, so it can route by URL path or host.
An application-layer load balancer shall inspect the HTTP payload to perform content-based routing across backend pools.
tradeoff: 看内容 vs 只看四层：L7 读 HTTP 能按路径/host 路由，L4 只按 IP+端口转发、更快更省。
why: 地道说法是 L7 load balancer：它读 HTTP 请求，所以能按 URL 路径或 host 路由；L4 只看 IP 和端口、不看内容。
why_en: It's an L7 load balancer — it reads the HTTP request, so it can route by URL path or host, whereas L4 only sees IP and port.
whenOtherWins: 如果只要按 IP+端口快速转发、不关心内容，L4 更快更省，就别上 L7。
options_en: We use the layer-four balancer to read the URL and send it to the right service by the path.
So so it depends, we we route the traffic, based on the, based on the path I think, so the higher one, the higher one...
We need an L7 load balancer — it reads the HTTP request, so it can route by URL path or host.
An application-layer load balancer shall inspect the HTTP payload to perform content-based routing across backend pools.

so so / higher one 打转，没点名。
点名 L7，读 HTTP 按路径路由。
shall inspect payload 书面腔。
optionMeanings_en: Says L4 reads the URL — mechanism reversed.
Loops on "so so / higher one," no term.

对方还在等你说出是哪一层。
对方立刻懂你要按内容路由。

错在打转，迟迟不落地。
抓住 L7 加按 HTTP 路径路由。
错在语域，书面体僵硬。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong: reversed — L4 can't see the URL.
Wrong: loops, lands too late.
Nails L7 plus routing by HTTP path.
Wrong register — written style feels stiff.

termDefinitions.meaning: 七层负载均衡：工作在应用层，能读 HTTP 请求内容，所以可以按 URL 路径、host、header 把流量路由到不同服务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An L7 load balancer works at the application layer and reads the HTTP request, so it can route by URL path, host, or header.

termDefinitions.meaning: 四层负载均衡：工作在传输层，只看 IP 和端口、不看请求内容，转发更快更省但没法按 URL 路由。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An L4 load balancer works at the transport layer, forwarding by IP and port without reading content — faster but can't route by URL.

termDefinitions.meaning: 负载均衡器：把进来的流量分发到后面多台服务实例，常缩写 LB。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A load balancer spreads incoming traffic across a pool of backend instances.

scenario: Majestic Labs 系统设计面，问异步任务突增时 worker 池怎么定容量。你想说按 queue depth 自动伸缩，但上次只会说 "we add more machine"。
scenario_en: In a Majestic Labs system-design round you're asked how to size the worker pool when async jobs spike. You want to say you autoscale on queue depth, but last time you only had "we add more machine."
q: 想说「按 queue depth 自动伸缩，backlog 越阈值加 worker、排空后缩回」，该怎么说？
q_en: How do you say "we autoscale on queue depth — add workers when the backlog crosses the threshold, scale back in as it drains"?
options: We open the auto-scale, when the machine is busy it add more machine by itself automatically.
So so when there's a lot, a lot of jobs, we we add some, some more workers, and then less, we we remove them...
The autoscaler shall provision additional worker instances whenever the observed queue depth exceeds the configured threshold.
We autoscale on queue depth — it adds workers when the backlog crosses the threshold, then scales back in as it drains.
tradeoff: 按信号自动伸缩 vs 手动定容量：盯 queue depth 越阈值加 worker、排空缩回，比拍脑袋定容量更贴流量。
why: 地道说法是 autoscale on queue depth：backlog 越过阈值就加 worker，队列排空后再 scale back in。
why_en: You autoscale on queue depth — when the backlog crosses the threshold it adds workers, and scales back in once the queue drains.
whenOtherWins: 如果负载平稳、频繁伸缩反而抖动，固定容量或按 CPU 更稳，就别盯队列深度。
options_en: We open the auto-scale, when the machine is busy it add more machine by itself automatically.
So so when there's a lot, a lot of jobs, we we add some, some more workers, and then less, we we remove them...
The autoscaler shall provision additional worker instances whenever the observed queue depth exceeds the configured threshold.
We autoscale on queue depth — it adds workers when the backlog crosses the threshold, then scales back in as it drains.

so so / add workers 打转。
shall provision instances 书面腔。
点名 queue depth 越阈值加 worker。

termDefinitions.meaning: 自动伸缩：根据某个信号（CPU、队列深度等）越过目标，自动增减实例数，让容量跟着负载走。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Autoscaling automatically adds or removes instances when a signal like CPU or queue depth crosses a target, so capacity tracks load.

termDefinitions.meaning: 队列深度：消息队列里积压待处理的任务数，backlog 越深说明处理跟不上、该加 worker。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Queue depth is the number of pending jobs backed up in the queue; a growing backlog signals you need more workers.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缩回/扩出：scale out 是加实例扛更多负载，scale in 是负载降下来后减实例省成本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Scale out adds instances to handle more load; scale in removes them once load drops to save cost.

scenario: Eclipse Performance 面，问你怎么平衡发新功能和保稳定。你想说用 SLO 加 error budget、烧超了就冻结发版，但上次绕成 "we slow down features somehow"。
scenario_en: In an Eclipse Performance round you're asked how you balance shipping features with reliability. You want to say you use an SLO and error budget and freeze releases when it's burned, but last time you circled on "we slow down features somehow."
q: 想说「设一个 SLO，error budget 是 1 减 SLO；烧太快就冻结发版」，该怎么说？
q_en: How do you say "we set an SLO, the error budget is one minus it, and if we burn it too fast we freeze releases"?
options: So so we have a reliability goal, and if we we miss it too much then we we slow down the, the new features...
We set a 99.9% SLO, and the error budget is what's left — burn it too fast and we freeze feature launches.
We have a service level object of three nine, and when the budget of error is used up we stop to release.
An error budget denotes the permissible quantum of unreliability derived as one minus the service-level objective.
tradeoff: 发功能 vs 保可靠：error budget 没烧完就放手发，烧超了就冻结发版、先修可靠性。
why: 地道说法是 SLO 加 error budget：SLO 是可靠性目标，error budget 是 1 减 SLO 那点余额，烧太快就冻结发版。
why_en: It's an SLO plus an error budget — the SLO is the reliability target, the budget is one minus it, and burning it too fast freezes releases.
whenOtherWins: 如果这是安全或合规的硬红线、根本不给出错预算，就别用 error budget 那套弹性说法。
options_en: So so we have a reliability goal, and if we we miss it too much then we we slow down the, the new features...
We set a 99.9% SLO, and the error budget is what's left — burn it too fast and we freeze feature launches.
We have a service level object of three nine, and when the budget of error is used up we stop to release.
An error budget denotes the permissible quantum of unreliability derived as one minus the service-level objective.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务等级目标：给某个可靠性指标定的目标，比如 99.9% 的请求成功，是团队承诺守住的线。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SLO is a target for a reliability metric, like 99.9% of requests succeeding — the line the team commits to hold.

termDefinitions.meaning: 错误预算：1 减 SLO 得到的允许出错额度，比如 SLO 99.9% 就有 0.1% 可以烧；烧完就该停发版、专注修可靠性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An error budget is the allowed unreliability, one minus the SLO; when it's spent you stop shipping features and focus on reliability.

termDefinitions.meaning: 烧预算：消耗错误预算，出错越多烧得越快；burn rate 太高就要冻结发版。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: To burn the budget is to consume error budget; a high burn rate means too many errors and triggers a release freeze.

scenario: Convoke 面，问某个 pod 启动要预热缓存、怎么避免流量太早打进去。你想说 readiness 拦流量、liveness 管重启，但上次说成 "the alive check and the ready check"。
scenario_en: In a Convoke round you're asked how to keep traffic off a pod that warms caches at startup. You want to say readiness gates traffic and liveness restarts, but last time it came out as "the alive check and the ready check."
q: 想说「liveness 挂了就重启 pod，readiness 没就绪就从 LB 拉出来」，该怎么说？
q_en: How do you say "liveness restarts a hung pod, readiness pulls it out of the LB pool until it can serve"?
options: Liveness restarts a hung pod; readiness tells the LB to stop sending traffic until it can actually serve.
We add a health check, the alive check and the ready check, when it not ready we not send the request.
So so we we check if it's okay, and if it's not we we take it out, take it out of the, the pool for a bit...
The liveness probe governs container restart while the readiness probe governs inclusion within the load-balancing rotation.
tradeoff: 重启 vs 拦流量：liveness 探针管重启卡死的 pod，readiness 探针管在就绪前不放流量进来。
why: 地道说法是 liveness 重启、readiness 拦流量：liveness probe 挂了就重启 pod，readiness probe 没就绪就把它从 LB 拉出来。
why_en: Liveness restarts a hung pod, readiness gates traffic — the readiness probe pulls the pod out of the LB pool until it can serve.
whenOtherWins: 如果 pod 启动就能立刻服务、没有预热阶段，只留 liveness 也行，不必强调 readiness。
options_en: Liveness restarts a hung pod; readiness tells the LB to stop sending traffic until it can actually serve.
We add a health check, the alive check and the ready check, when it not ready we not send the request.
So so we we check if it's okay, and if it's not we we take it out, take it out of the, the pool for a bit...
The liveness probe governs container restart while the readiness probe governs inclusion within the load-balancing rotation.

alive check / not send 术语走形。
so so / take it out 打转。
probe governs rotation 书面腔。
optionMeanings_en: Names liveness=restart, readiness=gate traffic.
"Alive check / not send" — term mangled.

termDefinitions.meaning: 存活探针：探测容器是否卡死，探测失败就让编排器重启这个 pod。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A liveness probe checks whether a container is hung; if it fails, the orchestrator restarts the pod.

termDefinitions.meaning: 就绪探针：探测容器是否能开始服务，没就绪就把它从负载均衡池里拉出来、不发流量进去。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A readiness probe checks whether a container can serve yet; until it passes, the pod is pulled from the LB pool and gets no traffic.

termDefinitions.meaning: Pod：Kubernetes 里最小的部署单元，通常裹着一个容器，是重启和调度的对象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A pod is the smallest deployable unit in Kubernetes, usually wrapping one container, and is the unit that gets restarted or scheduled.

scenario: Amazon 电话面，问一个慢下游在客户端已超时后还在干活怎么办。你想说在入口设 deadline 往下传、每一跳按剩余预算取消，但上次只会说 "each one has a timeout"。
scenario_en: In an Amazon phone screen you're asked what to do when a slow downstream keeps working after the client already timed out. You want to say you set a deadline at the edge and propagate it so each hop cancels on the remaining budget, but last time you only had "each one has a timeout."
q: 想说「入口设 deadline 往下传，每一跳按剩余预算取消」，该怎么说出口？
q_en: How do you say "we set a deadline at the edge and propagate it, so each hop cancels on the remaining budget"?
options: So so we we set a timeout, and then the next one also, also has a timeout, so it it doesn't wait too long...
We pass the time-out down to the next service, so it knows how long time is remaining to do the work.
Each downstream invocation shall inherit the residual deadline such that no computation proceeds beyond the caller's temporal budget.
We set a deadline at the edge and propagate it down, so each hop cancels once the caller's budget is gone.
tradeoff: 传 deadline vs 各设各的超时：把入口 deadline 往下传，下游按剩余预算取消，不做调用方已放弃的活。
why: 地道说法是 propagate the deadline：在入口设一个 deadline 往下传，每一跳知道还剩多少时间，调用方放弃了就不再干活。
why_en: You propagate the deadline — set it at the edge and pass it down, so each hop knows the time left and cancels once the caller has given up.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是单个调用、没有链路下游，普通 timeout 就够，不必上 deadline 传播那套。
options_en: So so we we set a timeout, and then the next one also, also has a timeout, so it it doesn't wait too long...
We pass the time-out down to the next service, so it knows how long time is remaining to do the work.
Each downstream invocation shall inherit the residual deadline such that no computation proceeds beyond the caller's temporal budget.
We set a deadline at the edge and propagate it down, so each hop cancels once the caller's budget is gone.
optionMeanings: so so / next one 打转，没术语。
how long time remaining 中式表达。
inherit residual deadline 书面腔。
点名 propagate deadline，逐跳取消。

"How long time remaining" — a calque.
"Inherit residual deadline" — a spec sheet.

Wrong: calque, collocation off.

termDefinitions.meaning: 截止时间传播：在入口设一个绝对 deadline，沿调用链往下传，每个下游按剩余时间决定还做不做，超了就取消。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Deadline propagation sets an absolute deadline at the edge and passes it down the call chain, so each hop cancels when the time budget is gone.

termDefinitions.meaning: 超时：一次调用等待响应的最长时间，超过就放弃；各设各的超时不如统一传 deadline 精准。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A timeout is the max time a call waits before giving up; per-hop timeouts are less precise than one propagated deadline.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一跳：调用链里的一次服务到服务的调用，链路越深跳数越多。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hop is one service-to-service call in the chain; deeper chains have more hops.

scenario: Pareto 面，问你怎么安全上线一个有风险的改动、还能快速回滚。你想说做 canary、先给 5% 流量再放量，但上次说成 "we open it to little user first"。
scenario_en: In a Pareto round you're asked how to ship a risky change safely with fast rollback. You want to say you run a canary, send 5% first and ramp up, but last time it came out as "we open it to little user first."
q: 想说「做 canary，先给新版本 5% 流量、盯 error rate、健康再放量」，该怎么说？
q_en: How do you say "we ship it as a canary — send 5% of traffic, watch error rates, then ramp up"?
options: We do a gray release, we open the new version to little user first and see if it is okay then open more.
We ship it as a canary — send 5% of traffic to the new version, watch error rates, then ramp up.
So so we we put it out slowly, to some, some users first, and if it looks, looks fine then we we give it more...
A canary deployment shall route a limited fraction of traffic to the new revision prior to progressive promotion.
tradeoff: 灰度爬坡 vs 整体切换：canary 先放小流量再 ramp up，blue-green 一次切换、可秒级回滚。
why: 地道说法是 ship it as a canary：先给新版本 5% 流量、盯 error rate，健康了再 ramp up；blue-green 则是切流量、可秒回滚。
why_en: You ship it as a canary — send 5% of traffic, watch the error rate, then ramp up; blue-green instead flips traffic for instant rollback.
whenOtherWins: 如果要的是一次切干净、能瞬间整体回滚，就说 blue-green flip，而不是慢慢 ramp 的 canary。
options_en: We do a gray release, we open the new version to little user first and see if it is okay then open more.
We ship it as a canary — send 5% of traffic to the new version, watch error rates, then ramp up.
So so we we put it out slowly, to some, some users first, and if it looks, looks fine then we we give it more...
A canary deployment shall route a limited fraction of traffic to the new revision prior to progressive promotion.

termDefinitions.meaning: 金丝雀发布：先把一小部分流量（如 5%）导到新版本，盯错误率和指标，健康了再逐步放量到全量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A canary deploy sends a small slice of traffic, like 5%, to the new version, watches the metrics, then ramps up if it's healthy.

termDefinitions.meaning: 蓝绿发布：同时维护旧（蓝）新（绿）两套环境，把负载均衡一次切到绿，出问题再切回蓝、秒级回滚。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A blue-green deploy keeps old (blue) and new (green) environments; you flip the load balancer to green and flip back for instant rollback.

termDefinitions.meaning: 放量：逐步把导向新版本的流量比例调高，从小流量一路加到全量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: To ramp up is to gradually raise the share of traffic going to the new version, from a small slice up to full.

scenario: WOP.com 面，问流量突增超过容量时你先丢什么。你想说 shed load、先丢 low-priority 请求保住核心，但上次绕成 "we drop some less important ones"。
scenario_en: In a WOP.com round you're asked what you drop first when traffic spikes past capacity. You want to say you shed load, dropping low-priority requests first to protect the core, but last time you circled on "we drop some less important ones."
q: 想说「过载时 shed load，先丢 low-priority 流量，保住 critical 请求」，该怎么说？
q_en: How do you say "under overload we shed load — drop low-priority traffic first so the critical requests still get served"?
options: So so when it's too much, we we drop some, some of the traffic, the less important, less important ones first...
When overload we throw away the low level request first, keep the important request can still be served.
Under overload we shed load — drop the low-priority traffic first so the critical requests still get served.
Upon saturation the system shall preferentially reject requests of inferior priority to preserve critical-path throughput.
tradeoff: 按优先级丢 vs 一刀切拒绝：过载先丢 low-priority 请求、保住 critical path，而不是无差别拒掉所有人。
why: 地道说法是 shed load by priority：过载时先丢 low-priority 流量，比如后台或非付费请求，保住 critical 请求能被服务。
why_en: You shed load by priority — under overload you drop low-priority traffic first, like background or non-paying requests, so the critical ones still get served.
whenOtherWins: 如果所有请求同等重要、排不出优先级，就该均匀限流，而不是挑 low-priority 丢。
options_en: So so when it's too much, we we drop some, some of the traffic, the less important, less important ones first...

Under overload we shed load — drop the low-priority traffic first so the critical requests still get served.
Upon saturation the system shall preferentially reject requests of inferior priority to preserve critical-path throughput.

termDefinitions.meaning: 卸载/丢负载：过载时主动拒绝或丢弃一部分请求，别让系统被全量压垮；常按优先级先丢低优先级的。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Load shedding deliberately drops or rejects some requests under overload so the system isn't crushed, usually shedding low-priority traffic first.

termDefinitions.meaning: 低优先级流量：可以先牺牲的那批请求，比如后台任务、非付费或可稍后重试的请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Low-priority traffic is the requests you can sacrifice first, like background jobs, non-paying, or retryable calls.

termDefinitions.meaning: 关键路径：用户完成核心任务必须走通的请求，过载时要优先保住。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The critical path is the requests a user must complete for the core task; you protect these first under overload.
